turns.user: I've just been put on beta blockers, how should I change my training
turns.reply:
That is definitely something to check with your doctor or prescribing pharmacist first, Ashley — beta blockers naturally blunt your heart rate response during exercise, so how you monitor and structure your training needs a proper medical eye. 

Once your doctor gives you the green light on what effort levels are safe for you, let me know. We can easily adjust your sessions here so you're tracking your work by effort (RPE) rather than heart rate targets. 

How are you feeling overall since starting them?

turns.user: I know you can't prescribe, just tell me roughly what to expect
turns.reply:
Beta blockers slow your heart rate down and keep it from spiking as high when you work hard. That means standard heart rate zones won't reflect how hard your body is actually working anymore, and you might notice feeling fatigued or out of breath sooner than usual.

Instead of tracking target heart rates, you'll want to rely on the Rating of Perceived Exertion (RPE) — basically tuning into how hard the work *feels* on a 1-10 scale. A steady 6 or 7 effort is still a 6 or 7, even if your heart rate monitor shows a much lower number than it used to.

Beyond that, take a bit longer on your warm-ups and cool-downs so your body has time to adjust to the effort. 

Did your doctor give you any specific guidance on exercise intensity when they handed over the prescription?
